title: Nocatee
name: Nocatee
metaDescription: Nocatee 1031 exchange scope covering master-planned town-center retail, new multifamily construction, and St. Johns County growth-corridor commercial parcels.

sections.html: Nocatee spans the St. Johns and Duval county line east of US-1, and it is one of the largest master-planned communities built in the metro over the past two decades. A scope narrative for this submarket has to account for a commercial base that is still being built out in real time rather than a mature, settled corridor.

sections.heading: A Town Center Still Filling In
sections.html:
Nocatee Town Center anchors the community's retail and service commercial, and new parcels within the development continue to come online as residential phases build out, which means a scope of work here should confirm exactly which phase a given parcel belongs to and what infrastructure is already in place versus still under construction. Buyers accustomed to a fully built suburban corridor should expect a different pace of change here, since new competing retail can enter the market during the holding period in a way that would not happen in an older, land-locked submarket.

A master developer continues to control much of the remaining land within Nocatee, and that single-ownership structure means new retail and commercial releases follow a planned sequence rather than the more scattered pattern typical of infill development, which a buyer can actually use to forecast competing supply with more precision than in most growth submarkets.

sections.heading: What Actually Trades in This Submarket
sections.html:
The identification candidates most common on a Nocatee scope narrative are:

  • grocery-anchored and lifestyle-retail centers within Nocatee Town Center
  • freestanding quick-service and bank-branch pad sites along the development's arterial roads
  • medical-office and urgent-care buildings serving new residential phases
  • newer multifamily and build-to-rent parcels adjacent to commercial nodes
  • self-storage and service-retail sites on the community's outer edges

A scope of work should note which of these categories has already stabilized versus which remain in initial lease-up, since the two carry meaningfully different income-projection risk in an appraisal narrative.

sections.heading: Demand Tied to an Unusually Fast Build-Out Pace
sections.html:
Nocatee's residential absorption has run faster than most master-planned communities in the state, and that pace is the clearest demand signal for a retail or multifamily replacement property in this submarket. A rent-roll or pro forma review should confirm whether projected rents assume the current build-out pace continuing at the same rate, since a slowdown in new home closings would directly affect retail sales volume and lease renewal strength for tenants inside the town center.

Household income within Nocatee also skews above the broader St. Johns County average, which supports a different tenant mix than a typical rooftop-driven suburban corridor, and a demand narrative should note that a national retailer selecting this location is underwriting both population growth and income profile together rather than population alone.

sections.heading: Procurement Watchouts for a Development-Phase Market
sections.html:
Community development district assessments are a standard feature of Nocatee parcels, and a buyer's diligence should confirm the exact CDD debt balance and annual assessment tied to a specific property rather than rely on a general figure for the development. Because the town center is still being built out, buyers should also confirm entitlement status on any adjacent undeveloped land, since a competing retail parcel approved nearby can affect an existing tenant's performance during the holding period.

Given the straddled county line, title and permitting review should confirm whether a specific parcel falls under St. Johns County or Duval County jurisdiction before finalizing a scope narrative.

sections.heading: Positioning Nocatee on an Identification List
sections.html:
Given its growth-stage profile, a Nocatee candidate often pairs well with a steadier, fully built-out submarket like Southside or Mandarin on a three-property identification list, balancing upside potential against a more predictable, settled asset. Ponte Vedra Beach is the closest comparable submarket for buyers seeking a similar demographic profile with a more mature commercial base.

Buyers should also confirm with their qualified intermediary how a Nocatee parcel's CDD assessment factors into the purchase price and basis calculation, since an assumed bond obligation can affect the net proceeds available for reinvestment differently than a straightforward fee-simple purchase without any assessment attached.

Lenders reviewing a Nocatee submittal will typically request the master developer's current phasing plan alongside a standard appraisal, since projected competing supply from future phases is a more material underwriting factor here than in a submarket where the surrounding land is already fully entitled and built.

faqs.q: Is Nocatee's commercial corridor fully built out yet?
faqs.a: No, new parcels continue to come online as residential phases complete, so a scope of work should confirm which phase a specific parcel belongs to and what infrastructure is already in place.

faqs.q: What drives retail demand in Nocatee?
faqs.a: An unusually fast residential build-out pace is the clearest demand signal, and a pro forma review should confirm whether projected rents assume that pace continuing, since a slowdown would directly affect tenant sales and renewals.

faqs.q: Do Nocatee properties carry community development district assessments?
faqs.a: Most do. A buyer's diligence should confirm the exact CDD debt balance and annual assessment tied to the specific parcel rather than relying on a general figure quoted for the development as a whole.

faqs.q: Which county governs a given Nocatee parcel?
faqs.a: It depends on location, since the development straddles the St. Johns and Duval county line, so title and permitting review should confirm the correct jurisdiction before finalizing a scope narrative.

faqs.q: What backup markets pair well with a Nocatee identification?
faqs.a: Southside or Mandarin offer a steadier, fully built-out alternative, while Ponte Vedra Beach offers a comparable demographic and income profile with a more mature commercial base already in place.
